title: Anthropic's Digital God, Pope vs AI, Job Loss Narrative Flips, Open Source Crackdown Coming?
thesis: The besties and Bill Gurley argue that AI's real danger is centralization of power — whether via Anthropic's 'safety' branding driving regulatory capture or a government ban on open-source models — while the job-apocalypse narrative is collapsing into a story about high-agency adoption and corporate over-hiring.

title: SpaceX Lowers IPO Valuation Target | Bloomberg Tech 5/29/2026
thesis: A week of record AI-driven valuations — SpaceX trimming its IPO target to $1.8T, Anthropic eclipsing OpenAI at $965B, Dell's blowout server guide — tests whether investors are paying for present fundamentals or a decade-out dream, with Blue Origin's exploded rocket as a reminder the dream isn't guaranteed.

title: Inference, Diffusion, World Models, and More | YC Paper Club
thesis: Five researchers walk through frontier papers showing that the next gains in AI come less from bigger pretraining and more from rethinking the stack — parallelizing inference for capability, factorized diffusion world models for control, elegant anti-collapse regularizers, classical generalization theory, and trading infinite compute for scarce data.

title: SpaceX's $2T Case, Nvidia's Shock Selloff, America Turns on AI, Trump Pulls AI Order, Bond Crisis?
thesis: AI economics have flipped from speculative to undeniably profitable — Anthropic is EBIT-positive and SpaceX's S-1 reveals a $15B/yr compute-rental business — yet public sentiment, geopolitics, and a brewing bond crisis are turning into the real constraints on the boom.

title: Elon's Anthropic Deal, The Next AI Monopoly?, "FDA for AI" Panic, Trading the AI Boom
thesis: SpaceX leasing its Colossus data center to Anthropic reveals that AI revenue is gated by power and compute—not demand—and signals both Elon's emergence as a hyperscaler and Anthropic's trajectory toward an unprecedented, politically combustible monopoly.

title: Yann LeCun's $1B Bet Against LLMs
thesis: LeCun argues that LLMs are a dead-end for general intelligence and that JEPA — a non-generative, joint-embedding world-model architecture — is the right substrate for agents that can predict the consequences of their actions.

title: Jensen Huang – Will Nvidia's moat persist?
thesis: Nvidia's moat isn't one thing — it's the whole five-layer stack (supply chain, chips, CUDA, ecosystem, install base) compounding annually. The TPU/ASIC threat is overstated, the China export-control debate is being fought on cartoon premises, and the next leg of compute scaling comes from algorithms and segmentation, not just transistors.

title: Jensen Huang: Nvidia's Future, Physical AI, Rise of the Agent, Inference Explosion, AI PR Crisis
thesis: Jensen Huang argues Nvidia has evolved from a GPU company into an AI-factory company whose moat is the full CUDA stack across every compute layer, and that agentic AI plus physical AI represent a vastly larger market than analysts model — so the industry's real risk is self-inflicted doomerism, not technology.

title: Richard Sutton – Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end
thesis: Turing Award winner Richard Sutton argues LLMs are a conceptual dead-end because they mimic human outputs without a goal, ground truth, or world model, and that true intelligence will come from agents that learn continually from experience — and that succession to designed AI is inevitable and worth embracing.

title: AI can't cross this line and we don't know why.
thesis: Neural scaling laws describe a startlingly simple power-law relationship between compute, data, model size and model loss — and the manifold hypothesis offers a compelling but incomplete theoretical reason why this 'compute-efficient frontier' exists at all.

title: Demis Hassabis — Scaling, superhuman AIs, AlphaZero atop LLMs, AlphaFold
thesis: Hassabis argues the most likely path to AGI is large multimodal models used as world-model priors with AlphaZero-style planning and search bolted on top — and that DeepMind is roughly on the 20-year timeline it set in 2010.
